findings.title: enableSqlExpressions() contains dead, misleading logic that always returns false
findings.body: The new helper `enableSqlExpressions` computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` and then both the `if enabled` branch and the fallthrough path return `false`. The computed `enabled` value is never actually used to decide the return value — the function unconditionally returns `false` no matter what the feature toggle is set to. While the net effect (always disabling SQL expressions) matches the PR's stated goal, the code reads as if it is checking the feature flag when it is not, and there is no comment explaining that this is an intentional, permanent kill-switch. A future contributor who 'simplifies' this apparent dead code (e.g. by returning `enabled` directly) could unknowingly re-enable the vulnerable code path review intended to permanently disable. This should either be a plain `return false` with an explanatory comment referencing the CVE, or the SQL query type should be removed from the switch entirely.

findings.title: No tests added for the new SQL-expressions kill switch, and existing tests likely broken
findings.body: This PR fundamentally changes SQL expression behavior (TablesList/RunCommands/QueryFramesInto now always return "not implemented", and ReadQuery now always errors for QueryTypeSQL), but none of the changed files are tests. Given there must be pre-existing tests exercising pkg/expr/sql/parser.go (TablesList) and pkg/expr/sql_command.go (NewSQLCommand/Execute) that previously asserted correct DuckDB-based behavior (e.g. extracting table names, running real queries), those tests would now fail against the stubbed-out DB that always returns errors, since they are not included/updated in this diff. Conversely, no new test verifies that SQL expressions are now reliably blocked regardless of the FlagSqlExpressions toggle value (i.e., a regression test for the security fix itself is missing). For a PR whose entire purpose is to close an RCE/LFI vulnerability, lacking a test asserting the vulnerable path is unreachable is a significant gap that risks silent regression in future refactors.

findings.title: Error message "sqlExpressions is not implemented" is misleading
findings.body: When QueryTypeSQL is requested, ReadQuery now returns the error "sqlExpressions is not implemented". This is factually incorrect — SQL Expressions were implemented and are being deliberately disabled for security reasons (RCE/LFI, per CVE-2024-9264), not because the feature was never built. Users/administrators who previously had FlagSqlExpressions enabled and relied on it will see a confusing message implying the feature never existed, rather than a clear message indicating it has been disabled. This can misdirect support/debugging efforts and should be reworded (and ideally referenced in release notes/changelog, since this is a breaking change for anyone who had the toggle on).

findings.title: Leftover "duckDB" variable name contradicts stated PR goal of removing DuckDB references
findings.body: The PR description states the goal is to "Remove reference to DuckDB", yet the local variable in TablesList is still named `duckDB` (`duckDB := NewInMemoryDB()`) even though it now constructs the stub `sql.DB`, not a DuckDB instance. This is purely cosmetic but is inconsistent with the PR's own stated intent and could confuse future readers into thinking real DuckDB code still exists here.
